node-1.label: Ophthalmoscopic examination revealed a yellowish oval lesion within a wide area of chorioretinal atrophy

node-2.label: Patient has high myopia; axial length measured 30.0 mm

why.why: Radiologist analysis of OCT shows focal scleral ectasia with choroidal obliteration and thinning, matching the yellowish lesion seen clinically, and FA shows only mild late hyperfluorescence without neovascular leakage. These imaging findings directly confirm pathologic myopia degeneration and argue against active CNV or tumor. Combined with high myopia and axial length 30.0 mm, confidence increased from 0.65 to 0.92.

FA shows only mild late hyperfluorescence without neovascular leakage or tumor vascularity, and OCT demonstrates choroidal thinning and obliteration rather than a mass lesion. These findings argue strongly against choroidal neoplasm/tumor. Although high myopia is a weak risk factor, there is no direct tumor evidence, so confidence is reduced from 0.25 to 0.05.

No inflammatory or infectious evidence is present, and high myopia with axial elongation is the dominant explanation. OCT/FA findings are consistent with degenerative myopic changes rather than active choroiditis, so confidence is reduced from 0.1 to 0.03.
